steps.say: In Ebstein anomaly the tricuspid valve is built too low. The septal and posterior leaflets are displaced downward into the right ventricle by at least 8 millimetres per square metre of body surface area. That single measurement separates true Ebstein anomaly from a merely low lying but normal valve.
steps.tx: **Ebstein anomaly anatomy** features downward apical displacement of the **septal and posterior leaflets** of the tricuspid valve by at least **8 mm/m2** body surface area. The anterior leaflet is usually large and sail like, the valve leaks severely, and echocardiography must index the displacement to body size because absolute millimetres mislead in small infants.

steps.say: The displaced valve redraws the map of the right ventricle. The chamber above the leaflets becomes thin and atrialised, beating with the atrium instead of the ventricle. Only the small outlet chamber below remains as a working functional right ventricle, and it is often too small to sustain the pulmonary circulation alone.
steps.tx: Apical displacement partitions the ventricle into a thinned dysfunctional **atrialised right ventricle** and a small **functional right ventricle**. The atrialised portion balloons with severe tricuspid regurgitation and generates atrial arrhythmias, while the tiny functional chamber struggles to pump forward, so output depends on the size of the remaining effective ventricle.

points: Thin wall beating with the right atrium
Source of atrial flutter and fibrillation
left.title: Atrialised Portion

points: Small outlet chamber below the displaced valve
Only effective pumping part of the ventricle
Too small means cyanosis and low output
right.title: Functional Portion

steps.say: No other newborn chest film looks quite like severe Ebstein anomaly. Massive tricuspid leakage inflates the right atrium until the cardiac shadow touches both chest walls, the classic wall to wall heart. Newborns with this picture are deeply cyanosed and need prostaglandin to keep the duct open while surgeons plan.
steps.tx: The **wall-to-wall heart** on chest radiography marks extreme cardiomegaly from a huge right atrium distended by torrential tricuspid regurgitation. The silhouette can obscure the lung fields entirely in severely affected newborns, who present with profound cyanosis, a triple or quadruple rhythm, and duct dependent pulmonary flow requiring prostaglandin infusion.

vis.alt: Cardiac MRI showing severely dilated right ventricle with VSD patch and severe pulmonary regurgitation jet.
vis.caption: Severely dilated right heart chambers resembling the massive right sided enlargement of Ebstein anomaly. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: One psychiatric drug carries a famous cardiac warning. First trimester lithium exposure raises the relative risk of Ebstein anomaly in the fetus. Any woman with bipolar illness who takes lithium needs preconception counselling, a planned switch where possible, and a detailed fetal echocardiogram around 18 to 22 weeks.
steps.tx: **Maternal lithium exposure** in the first trimester carries an increased relative risk of **Ebstein anomaly**, the classic teratogenic association taught for this drug. The absolute risk stays small despite the raised relative risk, so management centres on preconception planning, the lowest effective strategy for maternal stability, and targeted fetal echocardiography rather than panic.

nodes.label: Woman with bipolar illness plans pregnancy while taking lithium
Preconception review weighs relapse risk against first trimester Ebstein risk
Detailed fetal echocardiography follows at 18 to 22 weeks gestation
Postnatal cardiology confirms valve anatomy and plans repair timing

steps.say: Ebstein anomaly and Wolff Parkinson White syndrome are linked together. Accessory pathways, usually right sided, are seen in 20 to 30 percent of patients and trigger atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia. Ablation is trickier here because the true annulus sits far from where the displaced valve appears to be.
steps.tx: **Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome** complicates Ebstein anomaly through accessory conduction pathways in up to **20-30%** of patients, predominantly **right sided** pathways that sustain orthodromic tachycardia. The short PR interval with delta wave on resting ECG should be sought in every Ebstein patient, and catheter ablation must map the true atrioventricular groove rather than the displaced valve hinge.

vis.alt: A 12 lead ECG labeled Wolff Parkinson White pattern shows normal rhythm with an inset magnifying a short PR interval, a slurred delta wave takeoff, and a wide QRS complex.
vis.caption: Short PR interval with delta wave marking an accessory pathway as seen in Ebstein anomaly. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: Tricuspid atresia leaves blood with no door into the right ventricle. The tricuspid orifice is completely absent, so survival demands an atrial septal defect for venous blood to cross leftward plus a ventricular septal defect or a patent ductus for blood to reach the lungs. A baby missing any link in this chain collapses early.
steps.tx: **Tricuspid atresia obligatory shunts** keep the circulation alive despite complete agenesis of the **tricuspid orifice**. An **obligatory ASD** lets systemic venous blood cross to the left atrium for mixing, while a **VSD or PDA** supplies pulmonary blood flow, so restrictive shunts at either level precipitate profound cyanosis and demand urgent balloon septostomy or surgical shunting.

nodes.label: Systemic veins return to a right atrium with no tricuspid exit
Blood crosses an obligatory ASD into the left atrium and mixes
Mixed blood reaches the lungs only through a VSD or PDA
Restriction at either shunt deepens cyanosis and forces urgent relief

steps.say: One tracing stands alone among cyanotic newborns. Tricuspid atresia is the single major cyanotic congenital defect that shows left axis deviation with left ventricular hypertrophy on the infant ECG. Every other cyanotic lesion points the axis rightward, so this leftward axis in a blue baby is practically diagnostic.
steps.tx: **ECG in tricuspid atresia** uniquely shows **left axis deviation** with **left ventricular hypertrophy** in a cyanosed infant, the only major cyanotic lesion to do so. The left ventricle does double work as the single pumping chamber and hypertrophies accordingly, while diminished right sided forces and a superior QRS vector complete a bedside diagnosis that echocardiography then confirms.

steps.say: A heart with no tricuspid valve can never support two separate circulations. Staged univentricular palliation carries these children from a newborn shunt through a Glenn to the final Fontan, where vena caval blood flows passively into the pulmonary arteries. The single left ventricle is then reserved entirely for the body.
steps.tx: Tricuspid atresia cannot support a biventricular circulation and follows the staged **Fontan single ventricle pathway**. A neonatal systemic to pulmonary shunt secures lung flow, the bidirectional Glenn connects the superior vena cava at 4 to 6 months, and the **Fontan completion** routes inferior caval blood to the lungs, leaving the single ventricle to pump to the body alone.

points: Two ventricles each serving one circulation
Possible when both AV valves are patent
Anatomical repair restores normal series flow
left.title: Biventricular Repair

points: Single ventricle reserved for the systemic circulation
Shunt to Glenn to Fontan staged palliation
Passive venous flow feeds the lungs without a pump
right.title: Fontan Pathway
